_howto: To publish a video: upload it to the team YouTube channel, then paste the video ID (the part after watch?v=) into "youtube". Leave it empty to show 'Coming soon'. Set channel.url to the channel link.

student.title: What is SPHEREx?
student.summary: A telescope that photographs the whole sky in 102 infrared colours, every six months.

student.title: Blinking: how Pluto was found
student.summary: Two photographs, one dot that moved. The idea behind the whole site.

student.title: Your first blink: Barnard's Star
student.summary: Load a field, play the survey passes, click the star that moves and read off how far it went.

student.title: Hidden in the noise: stacking
student.summary: WISE 0855 is invisible in one exposure. Average a whole pass and it appears.

student.title: Reading a spectrum
student.summary: Why a cold brown dwarf glows at 4.5 µm and a star does not, and how to tell them apart.

student.title: Could we find Planet X?
student.summary: How bright a distant planet would be, why SPHEREx cannot see it, and what could.

teacher.title: Teacher guide: running a blink lesson
teacher.summary: How the site works, what to prepare, and how to share a field or a mission with the class by link.

teacher.title: Lesson plan: moving stars (45 min)
teacher.summary: Students find Barnard's Star by blinking and measure its speed across the sky.

goals: Explain why nearby stars move across the sky
Measure an angle on a real image
Compare a measurement with a catalogue
steps: 10 min: show how Pluto was found by blinking (video 2)
15 min: practice mission 'The fastest star' in pairs
10 min: read the 'Did it move?' panel: measured vs catalogue
10 min: discussion: what limits our accuracy? (pixel size, parallax)

teacher.title: Lesson plan: invisible objects (45 min)
teacher.summary: Stacking makes the coldest known brown dwarf appear; the spectrum shows what it is.

goals: Use stacking to see faint objects
Use a spectrum to identify an object
steps: 15 min: spectral fingerprint of WISE 0855 vs a field star
5 min: exit question: why is it brightest at 4.5 µm?

teacher.title: Lesson plan: searching for Planet X (45 min)
teacher.summary: From real data to an honest conclusion: what SPHEREx can and cannot find.

goals: Estimate the brightness of a distant planet
Explain how injection tests prove a method works
steps: 10 min: calculator with the class: change distance and albedo
15 min: injection test on the Barnard field: where does completeness drop?
10 min: Track Pluto and look at its parallax loops
10 min: debate: is Planet X out there, and how would we find it?
